data.title: Abiemnom Massacre: Amnesty Faults South Sudan and UN Peacekeepers - Diplomacy and Law
data.content: # Abiemnom Massacre: Amnesty Faults South Sudan and UN Peacekeepers. The Abiemnom massacre of March 1, 2026, left a reported 213 people dead and at least 109 injured after an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 armed men attacked a town in South Sudan’s Ruweng Administrative Area. An investigation published by Amnesty International on November 11, 2026, concluded that South Sudanese authorities had received advance warnings but failed to take adequate measures to protect the population (Amnesty International, 2026). The investigation also raised serious questions about the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS). Peacekeepers stationed in Abiemnom knew that violence was becoming increasingly likely, and approximately 1,000 civilians had sought protection outside their temporary operating base the day before the massacre. South Sudan has binding human rights obligations to protect the lives and security of people within its jurisdiction, including against reasonably foreseeable violence by armed groups.
